study type: Critical Review and Re-analysis of Publicly Available Datasets
outcome: presence of specific Amplicon Sequence Variants (ASVs)
cohort: The study involved the re-analysis of data from 15 publicly available 16S rRNA gene datasets, focusing on human term placentas.
finding: Contemporary DNA-based evidence, after accounting for likely DNA contaminant removal and mode of delivery, does not support the existence of a placental microbiota in term placentas.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery profoundly influenced the bacterial DNA signal from term-delivered placentas, with Lactobacillus prevalence disappearing after contaminant removal in placentas from term cesarean deliveries.
